evidence_summary: Clark-branded units carry a Manufactured and Distributed by Clark Music Industries statement, while former Clark employee Rich Excellente described wiring fuzz boxes at the three-person Clark Electronics operation in Clark, New Jersey. This strongly supports Clark involvement and builder status for the Clark-branded state, while the broader East Coast family remains unresolved.

A January 18 1968 Cleveland newspaper advertisement establishes Manny's Fuzz in legitimate retail distribution, but current evidence does not identify the physical factory. It should not be assigned to Clark solely from family resemblance.

A September 13 1968 St. Louis Post-Dispatch classified documents an Orpheum Fuzz in circulation. Fuzzboxes identifies Orpheum as one of the known East Coast Fuzzrite-family marketed identities, but physical builder remains unresolved.

Fuzzboxes lists the Boston E.U. Wurlitzer Fuzzer Buzzer among the East Coast Fuzz identities. A surviving late-1960s example has a 20th-week-1967 pot code, but a marketplace listing's claim of Apollo/Orpheum Japanese production is seller-level evidence and is not treated as factory attribution.

Effects Database groups MGI Fuzz with Clark, E.U. Wurlitzer, Halifax, Orpheum, Manny's, Mica-Tone, Andre and AAT states. A 2009 specialist forum identifies MGI as the same family as Orpheum and others, but does not establish the physical factory.
Fuzzboxes identifies Andre Fuzzier as an East Coast marketed identity founded by Gene Andre in New Jersey. Current evidence supports family membership but not a physical-builder assignment.

Fuzzboxes and Effects Database identify Gracin's Fubar as an East Coast family member. Fuzzboxes notes that the link to Bernie Gracin's New York music-store chain remains unconfirmed, so both branding and factory remain open questions.
Effects Database groups Mica-Tone with the Orpheum and Manny's forms. The current evidence supports family identity only and does not identify a physical manufacturer.
Effects Database and specialist forum evidence place AAT Fuzzier in the same East Coast family as Orpheum, Manny's, Andre and related variants. Physical builder remains unknown.
Effects Database groups Tim's Own Fuzzer Buzzer with Orpheum and MGI variants. No independent physical-builder attribution was found in the current evidence set.
